name: Alex Rivera
summary: Senior Software Engineer with 8+ years building and operating backend services in Python and Go. Led the design of an event-driven order platform handling 12M requests per day, mentored five engineers, and cut cloud spend by 31% through targeted performance work. Comfortable owning a system from design review through on-call.

items.label: Services & APIs
items.value: REST, gRPC, GraphQL, Kafka, event-driven architecture, microservices

items.label: Infrastructure
items.value: AWS (ECS, Lambda, SQS, RDS), Kubernetes, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Datadog

items.label: Practices
items.value: System design, code review, mentoring, observability, incident response, agile delivery

roles.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Designed an event-driven order orchestration service on Kafka and Go that processes 12M requests per day with 99.95% availability.
Cut monthly cloud spend by 31% (about $240K a year) by right-sizing workloads, adding caching, and removing a redundant data pipeline.
Led a four-engineer migration of a legacy monolith module to gRPC services with zero customer-facing downtime.
Mentored five engineers and ran the team's design review process, reducing production incidents tied to design gaps by 40%.
Defined service-level objectives and alerting for 14 services, replacing noisy pager rules and reducing after-hours pages by 55%.
Drove adoption of a shared Go service template used by nine teams, cutting new service setup from two weeks to two days.
Partnered with finance and operations to model peak-season load, then load-tested the platform to 3x expected traffic before launch.
Wrote the internal guide on safe schema migrations and zero-downtime deploys, now the standard reference for backend engineers across the company.
Evaluated build-versus-buy options for the notification platform and recommended a managed service, avoiding roughly six engineer-months of work.

roles.title: Software Engineer II
bullets: Built the carrier rate-shopping API in Python and FastAPI, trimming median response time from 900 ms to 210 ms.
Introduced contract testing across six services, catching breaking changes before release and halving rollback frequency.
Owned the on-call runbook rewrite, cutting mean time to resolve incidents from 52 to 28 minutes.
Implemented idempotent webhook delivery with retries and dead-letter queues, eliminating duplicate shipment notifications.
Migrated the reporting database to a read replica and partitioned tables, dropping dashboard query times from 40 seconds to 3.
Interviewed 30+ candidates and onboarded four new hires with a structured first-90-days plan.
Added structured logging and distributed tracing to the order pipeline, making cross-service debugging practical for the whole team.
Built a feature flag system with gradual rollouts that let the team ship daily with confidence.

roles.title: Software Engineer
bullets: Developed inventory sync services in Python and PostgreSQL used by 400+ stores, replacing nightly batch jobs with near-real-time updates.
Automated release pipelines with GitHub Actions and Terraform, shrinking deploy time from 2 hours to 15 minutes.
Partnered with product and support teams to triage customer-reported defects, closing 90% within the agreed service level.
Built a Python tool that reconciled point-of-sale and warehouse counts, flagging discrepancies that saved an estimated $60K in shrinkage per year.
Introduced code review checklists and pair programming sessions, improving first-pass review approval rate from 55% to 80%.
Rebuilt the store-facing price update service to support promotional schedules, removing a weekly manual process for the merchandising team.
Reduced flaky test failures from 18% to under 2% by isolating shared fixtures and containerizing integration tests.
Presented quarterly architecture updates to engineering leadership and gathered feedback from store operations.

roles.title: Software Engineer Intern
bullets: Built an internal dashboard in React and Flask that surfaced build health for 30 engineers.
Added automated alerts for failed builds, which the team adopted as its default workflow.

sections.title: Education
lines: B.S. Computer Science, Prairie State University, Springfield, IL, 2016 (GPA 3.7)
